Binomial / Poisson Cumulative

Single-term and range probabilities for Bin(n,p) and Po(λ). 110 bytes.

keys
MODE→6→2

nCr types one binomial term; a CDF is a loop. This WebCal version II listing auto-detects the law: if the second input is a probability in (0,1) it is Binomial (then n, p, k); otherwise it is Poisson (λ, k). Enter an upper index at the next prompt for P(k ≤ X ≤ m). EXE through extra terms, then 0 EXE to print the sum. AC after a one-term run. nCr is SHIFT ÷. On the fx-50FH II the × after nCr may be omitted (109 bytes) and A^(B)÷B!e^(A needs no extra brackets.

note

110 bytes (109 on fx-50FH II) of the shared 680-byte pool. Create the slot in COMP. Type ? → : ◢ Goto Lbl If Then from SHIFT 3 (P-CMD).

formula
P(X=k)=C(n,k)pk(1−p)n−k

Program (one line)

basic
ClrMemory:?→A:?→B:B⇒1>B⇒B→Y:Ans⇒?→B:Lbl 0:Y⇒A nCr B Y^(B)(1-Y)^(A-B→C:Y=0⇒A^(B)÷B!e^(A→C:CM+:X=0⇒?→C:C≧1⇒C→X:1+B→B:X≧B⇒Goto 0:C⇒X=0⇒Goto 0:M

Example 1: X ~ Bin(9, 0.5), P(X = 4)

Question: Use this program to solve the case: X ~ Bin(9, 0.5), P(X = 4).

Given: Second input 0.5 is in (0,1), so the third prompt is k.

  1. 9 EXE 0.5 EXE 4 EXE
  2. Display ≈ 0.24609. AC to leave

Example 2: Same X, P(4 ≤ X ≤ 6)

Question: Use this program to solve the case: Same X, P(4 ≤ X ≤ 6).

Given: After k = 4, enter the upper index 6.

  1. 9 EXE 0.5 EXE 4 EXE 6 EXE
  2. Display 0.65625
  3. Or 4 EXE, EXE, EXE to see 0.24609, 0.24609, 0.16406, then 0 EXE for the sum

Example 3 (edge): X ~ Po(5), P(X = 4) and P(4 ≤ X ≤ 6)

Question: Use this program to solve the case: X ~ Po(5), P(X = 4) and P(4 ≤ X ≤ 6).

Given: Second input 4 is not a probability, so A is λ.

  1. 5 EXE 4 EXE → P(X=4) ≈ 0.17547, then AC
  2. 5 EXE 4 EXE 6 EXE → P(4≤X≤6) ≈ 0.49716
note

Do not enter p = 0 or p = 1 as the second input — those look like Poisson. P(X=0) for Poisson: λ EXE 0 EXE. The running sum lives in M. Source: WebCal binomial_PoissonDist2.htm.
